content.key_idea: Splitting an n x n matrix-vector product's n diagonals into n1 baby-step groups of n2 diagonals each cuts the needed ciphertext rotations from n down to about n1+n2 (here 3+2=5 vs 6), a saving that grows as O(sqrt(n)) instead of O(n) for larger matrices.
content.reading_order: left to right: the matrix and input vector, split into two coloured baby-step rotation groups (rotate diags down by 0/1 times n1), each group's n1 elementwise products, then giant-step 'rotate up' realignment, finally summed into the single result vector matching the diagonal method's answer

summary: This figure visualizes how Orion's use of the baby-step giant-step (BSGS) algorithm cuts the ciphertext rotations needed for a homomorphic matrix-vector product. Panel (a) shows the baseline diagonal method on a 6x6 matrix: all six generalized diagonals are each rotated and multiplied against the input vector, needing n=6 ciphertext rotations before the six partial products are summed into the result. Panel (b) shows the same 6x6 matrix computed via BSGS with n1=3, n2=2: the six diagonals are split into two colour-coded baby-step groups of three, each group needs only its own n1=3 rotations (shared across the group) to compute a partial sum, and then just n2=2 giant-step 'rotate up' operations realign the two groups' partial sums before they are added into the same final result vector as (a). By trading n total rotations for roughly n1+n2 rotations, BSGS reduces the matrix-vector product's rotation complexity from O(n) to O(sqrt(n)).
summary_zh: 该图展示Orion中BSGS算法如何减少同态矩阵-向量乘法所需的密文旋转次数：(a)对角线法对6x6矩阵的6条对角线各做1次旋转（共6次）后求和；(b)BSGS将对角线分成n1=3、n2=2两组，每组仅需n1次基线旋转，再用n2次巨步旋转对齐后相加，得到相同结果，将旋转次数从O(n)降到O(√n)。
